t: You're looking at one of a set of twenty-one benches along the Embankment pavement. They date from the late nineteenth century and have an Egyptian revival design. They were designed by the Vulliamy family of architects. George John Vulliamy also designed the pedestal and sphinxes for Cleopatra's Needle on the Embankment, and the sturgeon lamp posts that line it, so the Egyptian styling fits. Lewis Vulliamy, another architect from a family of clockmakers, is also credited with the design.
